newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Singapore shares ended lower on profit-taking in large capitalised stocks on Friday.

Dealers said investors wanted to close their positions ahead of the weekend and the release of key U.S. job employment data later today. Sentiment was also cautious following the big fall in Tokyo stocks where the Nikkei 225 average fell 770 points to end 17,303.65.
"Selling was mainly in the big cap stocks. The sharp fall in Japanese stocks may have forced some investors to liquidate their other holdings to cover losses," said an institutional dealer.
The Straits Times Industrial index ended down 11.42 points at 2,242.31. Volume was 182 million with 213 gainers and 178 losers.
Among the losers were index stocks Cycle & Carriage and Keppel Corp which shed and Singapore $0.50 (US$0.36) and S$0.20 respectively. DBS Bank foreign also shed 60 cents to S$19.10.
Dealers said retail interest in smaller issues and Malaysian speculative counters hogged the actives.
Most electronic issues took a breather after sharp gains this week but Wong's Circuits managed to close higher at US$1.27, up three cents.
